subject.title: fix: derived caches wedge cloud-worker reconciliation and reclaim

question: Should cloud-worker workspaces unconditionally exclude the proposed derived-path set, including `node_modules` and all `.pyc`/`.pyo` path segments, after live proof confirms reconciliation and reclaim behavior?
rationale: This changes the effective workspace-sync contract for existing cloud-worker users; focused tests establish implementation intent but cannot decide whether the fixed exclusion set is the desired product boundary.

options.title: Approve the fixed exclusion boundary
options.body: Accept the unconditional exclusion set after a redacted live run demonstrates successful reconciliation and reclaim following local derived-cache churn.

options.title: Narrow the invariant
options.body: Limit exclusions to the demonstrated cache classes if maintainers need dependency trees or bytecode-like paths to remain transferable in supported workflows.

recommendation.title: Approve the fixed exclusion boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the unconditional exclusion set after a redacted live run demonstrates successful reconciliation and reclaim following local derived-cache churn.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history ties this person directly to the cloud-worker incident analysis and the proposed repair, although current-main ownership was not independently verified.
